conventions: The paper's phi_S is written as ADROIT's Higgs doublet H; phi_D is named phiD.
Both doublets have hypercharge 1/2 in Q = T3 + Y (standard 2HDM normalization). <phi_S^0> = v/sqrt(2) with v = 246.22 GeV, the same as ADROIT's convention.
V enters L as -V. The paper's -1/2 m_ii^2 mass terms become +m_ii^2/2 coefficients in L.

The physical-mass relations used for the inversion are: M_H^2 = mu_2^2 + lambda_345 v^2/2; M_A^2 = mu_2^2 + (lambda_3 + lambda_4 - lambda_5) v^2/2; M_Hpm^2 = mu_2^2 + lambda_3 v^2/2; with mu_2^2 = -m22^2/2.
The quartics lambda_3, lambda_4, lambda_5 and the mass parameter m22^2 are written as formulas in the benchmark inputs M_H, M_A, M_Hpm and lambda_345. No numbers were computed.
assumptions: Tree-level relations are used throughout: lambda_1 = M_h^2/v^2 and m11^2 = M_h^2.
H, the CP-even neutral component of phi_D, is the dark matter, following the paper (lambda_5 < 0 for this benchmark).

agent_spec.name: inert_doublet_model_ee_benchmark
agent_spec.source: Kalinowski, Kotlarski, Robens, Sokolowska, Zarnecki, arXiv:1809.07712, eq. (2)

fields.name: H
fields.mass_justification: SM-like doublet phi_S; mass parameter and quartic given by explicit terms fixed by M_h and v

fields.name: phiD
fields.mass_justification: Inert doublet phi_D. Its Lagrangian mass parameter mu_2^2 = -m22^2/2 = M_H^2 - lambda_345 v^2/2 is a formula, so it is written as an explicit term. Its neutral CP-even component H (M_H = 72.77 GeV) is the dark matter.

couplings.name: M_H
couplings.justification: benchmark: dark matter mass (neutral scalar H)

terms.text: +(1/2) m11^2 (phi_S^dag phi_S), with m11^2 = lambda_1 v^2 = M_h^2
+(1/2) m22^2 (phi_D^dag phi_D), with -m22^2/2 = M_H^2 - lambda_345 v^2/2
-lambda_3 (phi_S^dag phi_S)(phi_D^dag phi_D), with lambda_3 = lambda_345 + 2(M_Hpm^2 - M_H^2)/v^2
-lambda_4 (phi_S^dag phi_D)(phi_D^dag phi_S), with lambda_4 = (M_A^2 + M_H^2 - 2 M_Hpm^2)/v^2

assumptions: The SM-like doublet's potential parameters are fixed at tree level by M_h and v: lambda_1 = M_h^2/v^2 and m11^2 = M_h^2.
All couplings are real; lambda_5 < 0, so H (CP-even) is the lightest dark particle, as the paper chooses.
The inert doublet does not couple to fermions, so there are no Yukawa terms for phiD.
agent_spec.stability: Exact Z2 (D-symmetry): phi_D -> -phi_D. Only phi_S takes a vev, so the lightest dark scalar H is stable.
agent_spec.cosmology: standard: radiation domination from a reheating temperature far above m_χ/20, Standard Model degrees of freedom, no late entropy release

conventions: The paper uses Q = T3 + Y, the same as ADROIT. The wino has Y = 0, so no conversion is needed.

The paper writes the Majorana triplet as a two-component Weyl spinor with the Lagrangian 1/2 chi (i sigmabar D - M_chi) chi. It is represented here as one self-conjugate (Majorana) four-component field. Its mass_gev is M in the term 1/2 M chi-bar chi, which equals the paper's M_chi.
The covariant derivative D_mu = d_mu - i g2 W^a T^a is taken to match ADROIT's gauge convention for the kinetic term. Only the triplet's SU(2) representation is specified.
assumptions: The benchmark mass of 2860 GeV is the paper's central thermal mass for the Majorana 3-plet.
No Standard Model fermion fields are listed, because no explicit term couples to them. Their gauge interactions with the W are implicit.

agent_spec.name: pure_wino_majorana_triplet
agent_spec.source: Bottaro, Buttazzo, Costa, Franceschini, Panci, Redigolo, Vittorio, 'Closing the window on WIMP Dark Matter', arXiv:2107.09688, Eq. (2), fermionic 3-plet

fields.name: chi
fields.mass_justification: Thermal freeze-out mass of the Majorana 3-plet from Table I (2.86 ± 0.01 TeV, with Sommerfeld enhancement and bound-state formation). It enters as M_chi in the Majorana mass term -1/2 M_chi chi chi of Eq. (2).

couplings.name: M_chi
couplings.justification: Benchmark dark matter mass of 2860 GeV (Table I, Majorana 3-plet).

assumptions: The model has only gauge interactions. The SU(2)_L coupling to W^a comes from the covariant derivative in the kinetic term, D_mu = d_mu - i g2 W^a T^a, which ADROIT generates from the field's charges. No explicit interaction terms are therefore listed.
The decay operator chi H L, allowed at the renormalizable level for the 3-plet, is forbidden by a Z2 symmetry acting on the dark sector, as the paper assumes. The field chi is given dark_parity -1.

The splitting between the charged and neutral components (about 167 MeV) is radiative, from gauge loops. It is not a tree-level Lagrangian input, so at tree level the multiplet is degenerate at M_chi.
The Higgs doublet is listed because the model contains an electroweak multiplet. The fermion triplet has no renormalizable coupling to H once the Z2 is imposed.
dropped: Dimension-7 operator c_f/Lambda_UV^3 chi^a chi^b (H^dag T^a H)(H^dag T^b H) of Eq. (5). It is non-renormalizable, and the paper gives no benchmark value for c_f or Lambda_UV; its contribution to the splitting is stated to be negligible.
agent_spec.stability: A Z2 under which chi is odd forbids the renormalizable decay operator chi H L. The neutral component of the triplet is the lightest state, because the radiative splitting raises the charged components.
agent_spec.cosmology: standard: radiation domination from a reheating temperature far above m_χ/20, Standard Model degrees of freedom, no late entropy release
